referenceFixtureNote: Rounded circular and transfer reference values use the explicit Earth radius and gravitational parameter in the frozen implementation. Conservation, boundary and residual checks exercise the actual exported physics functions. The benchmark reference is a rounded analytic value, not live celestial data.
assumptions: Earth-centered two-body Newtonian gravity with μ = 398600.4418 km³/s² and Earth radius 6378.137 km.
Coplanar, prograde circular endpoint orbits; two instantaneous tangential burns.
Kepler equation propagation on the transfer ellipse; circular analytic propagation before and after transfer.
Altitude input range 160 to 50000 km; no fuel mass conversion.
Diagram is top-down and scale-to-fit. Full transfer ellipse is shown for context; spacecraft travels half of it.
limitations: No drag, oblateness, third-body forces, finite burns, plane changes, launch dynamics, rendezvous, longitude or station keeping.
GEO is an altitude preset; no real-time Earth orientation or live data.
Equal-altitude missions have zero delta-v, but retain a half-period timeline.
Educational idealized transfer planning only; not operational flight guidance.
